title: Boss: ready for the team
summary: Make a fresh repo ready for the whole team in VS Code: settings, debugging, a dev container and remote access.

steps.title: Onboarding in one click
body: Your team adopts the `~/payments` service. Today a new developer needs a day to get it running, nobody can debug it the same way, and the staging box is reached by a copy-pasted SSH command.

The ticket: *a new hire clones the repo, clicks Reopen in Container, presses F5 and has a breakpoint hit within ten minutes.* Four files make that true. Write each as plain JSON (or SSH config) and check it with `jq` or `ssh -G` as you go.

steps.title: Shared settings and recommended extensions
prompt: 2. `.vscode/extensions.json`: recommend `ms-python.python` (`{ "recommendations": ["ms-python.python"] }`), so VS Code offers to install it to everyone who opens the folder.

checks.name: workspace settings are right
checks.fail: `~/payments/.vscode/settings.json` should set `editor.formatOnSave`, `files.eol` and a `[python]` block with `editor.tabSize` 4, as valid JSON.

hints: Check each with `jq . file` before you commit.
`cd ~/payments && git add .vscode && git commit -m "Share VS Code settings"`.
steps.explain: `extensions.json` recommends without forcing: VS Code shows a prompt, and the Extensions view lists them under *Recommended*.

steps.title: F5 starts the service
prompt: Add `~/payments/.vscode/launch.json` with one configuration named `Run payments`: `type` `debugpy`, `request` `launch`, `program` `${workspaceFolder}/src/app.py`, `args` `["--port", "8001"]`, `env` `{ "APP_ENV": "dev" }`, `console` `integratedTerminal`. Commit it.
Prove it starts: the configured command must print `listening on 8001 in dev`.

checks.name: the configuration is complete
checks.cmd: jq -e '.version == "0.2.0" and (.configurations[0] | .name == "Run payments" and .type == "debugpy" and .request == "launch" and .program == "${workspaceFolder}/src/app.py" and .args == ["--port", "8001"] and .env.APP_ENV == "dev")' ~/payments/.vscode/launch.json
checks.fail: Check every field of the configuration, and `"version": "0.2.0"` at the top.

checks.name: the configured command runs
checks.fail: Running the configured program with its args and env does not print `listening on 8001 in dev`.

steps.explain: A committed `launch.json` turns "how do I run this?" into F5. Keep secrets out of it: use `envFile` pointing at an ignored `.env` file for anything private.

steps.title: One toolchain, and the way to staging
prompt: 2. `~/.ssh/config`: a host `payments-staging` for Remote-SSH: `HostName staging.payments.example.com`, `User deploy`, `IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`, `IdentitiesOnly yes`, `ProxyJump bastion.example.com`, mode `600`. Check it with `ssh -G payments-staging`.

checks.name: the dev container is defined and committed
checks.cmd: cd ~/payments && jq -e '.name == "payments" and .image == "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12" and (.forwardPorts | index(8001)) != null and (.postCreateCommand | test("pip install -r requirements.txt"))' .devcontainer/devcontainer.json >/dev/null && git ls-files --error-unmatch .devcontainer/devcontainer.json >/dev/null && test -z "$(git status --porcelain .devcontainer)"
checks.fail: `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` should be valid JSON with the four fields, and committed.

checks.name: ssh resolves payments-staging
checks.fail: `ssh -G payments-staging` does not show the right host name, user, `IdentitiesOnly yes` and `ProxyJump` yet.

hints: The dev container is the same shape as in the lesson, with port 8001.
Append to the SSH config with `cat >> ~/.ssh/config <<'EOF'`: a `Host payments-staging` line and indented settings.
steps.explain: The repo now carries its own environment and debug setup, and your SSH config carries the way in. The new hire's ten minutes: clone, **Reopen in Container**, F5. For staging, **Remote-SSH: Connect to Host...** and pick `payments-staging`.
